name: Acne
summary: Active breakouts and old scarring respond to different treatments.
leadAnswer: Acne is a common skin condition in which pores become blocked with oil and dead skin, leading to blackheads, inflamed spots and sometimes scarring. Active acne is usually managed medically first, and energy-based treatment is considered for the marks and scars it leaves.
seoTitle: Acne Treatment in Malaysia: Types & Causes | Kaiteki
seoDescription: Active acne and acne scarring are different problems with different treatments. A doctor assesses which you have. Book a free consultation at Kaiteki.

banner.alt: Illustrative photograph: a woman in a white bathrobe touching her chin, with small blemishes on her cheek and jaw, against a plain off-white wall

facts.label: Affects up to 85% of people aged 12–24, and can continue or begin in adulthood.
Active breakouts and the marks or scarring left behind need different approaches.
Active inflamed acne is usually settled with topical or oral treatment before any device is considered.

sections.heading: What is acne?
body: Acne occurs when hair follicles become blocked with oil and dead skin cells. That blockage can stay quiet as a blackhead or whitehead, or it can become inflamed and form a red, tender spot.

drivers.heading: Common causes
drivers.intro: Usually several of these at once:

items.body: puberty, menstrual cycles, pregnancy, polycystic ovary syndrome, or stopping hormonal contraception.
oil glands producing more than the skin can clear, and dead skin cells building up inside the follicle instead of shedding.
Cutibacterium acnes multiplying in a blocked follicle and triggering redness and swelling.
family history, certain medications, occlusive skincare or makeup, humidity and sweat, friction from helmets, straps or masks.

variant.heading: Which type do I have?
variant.intro: Most people arrive with a mix. Working out the balance matters, because treating scarring while acne is still active usually does not work well, and treating active acne will not remove existing scars.

tabs.label: Active acne
tabs.title: Active acne
tabs.routing: medical management first, with clinic facials or RF microneedling considered as support once the doctor advises it.

tabs.label: Marks
tabs.title: Post-acne marks
tabs.body: Flat discolouration left after a spot heals. The skin is smooth; only the colour differs. Marks often fade on their own over months.

items.body: (post-inflammatory erythema), from dilated blood vessels near the surface. More visible on lighter skin.
(post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation), from excess pigment produced during inflammation. Very common in the medium and deeper skin tones seen across Malaysia, and worsened by sun exposure.

tabs.label: Scarring
tabs.title: Acne scarring
tabs.body: A change in the skin's structure you can feel as a dip or a raised area. Scars do not fade on their own.
tabs.routing: RF microneedling or resurfacing laser, often over several sessions, with combinations chosen by scar type.

locationBlock.heading: Where acne appears
locationBlock.intro: Location is a clue, not a diagnosis.

cards.title: Chin and jawline
cards.body: Often follows a hormonal pattern, particularly in adult women, and can flare in a monthly cycle.

cards.title: Forehead
cards.body: Commonly linked to oil, sweat, hair products and friction from caps, helmets or fringes.

cards.title: Cheeks
cards.body: Friction and contact are frequent contributors: phone screens, pillowcases, mask edges.

cards.title: Nose
cards.body: Dense oil glands mean blackheads and visible pores are common here.

cards.title: Back, chest and shoulders
cards.body: Sweat, friction and heavier body products play a part. Lesions here can be larger and are more likely to leave raised rather than depressed scars.

note.title: Not typical acne?
note.body: Small uniform bumps that itch, or rashes that do not respond to acne treatment, may be something else entirely, such as folliculitis or rosacea.

triggers: Over-the-counter products have not helped after around eight to twelve weeks of consistent use.
Spots are deep, painful or leaving marks behind.
Breakouts started in adulthood, or changed pattern suddenly.
Your acne is affecting your mood, confidence or how you go about your day.

ctaMid.heading: Not sure which one you're dealing with?
ctaMid.body: Send us a photo on WhatsApp and a doctor can tell you whether you're looking at active acne, marks, scarring, or a combination.

treatmentsIntro: Treatments considered for acne at Kaiteki, by what each addresses:

pico-laser.why: For post-acne marks and uneven tone
pico-laser.body: A picosecond laser that targets pigment in short, high-speed pulses.

microneedling.why: For depressed scarring, texture and enlarged pores
microneedling.body: Fine needles deliver radiofrequency energy into the deeper layer of the skin to stimulate collagen. Often the starting point for rolling and boxcar scarring, and generally considered a lower pigmentation-risk option for medium and deeper skin tones.

resurfacing-laser.why: For deeper scarring and significant texture change
resurfacing-laser.body: A fractional CO₂ laser used where scarring is more established. More downtime than the options above.

exosome-therapy.why: Used alongside other treatments, not instead of them
exosome-therapy.body: A regenerative approach applied after energy-based treatment to support skin recovery. The evidence base is still developing.

facial-treatments.why: For congestion, cleansing and ongoing maintenance
facial-treatments.body: Hydrafacial and Silkpeel are used to support cleansing and exfoliation, particularly with comedonal congestion. They do not replace medical treatment for inflammatory acne.

firstVisit.intro: The first job is telling apart what is active, what is marking and what is scarring.

steps.title: History
steps.body: What you've tried, and any medication or skincare you currently use.

steps.title: Examination
steps.body: The doctor examines your skin, sometimes under magnification.

steps.title: Discussion and plan
steps.body: Options, risks and downtime, with no obligation to proceed.

items.body: Redness, swelling, dryness, flaking and a warm or gritty sensation for a few days. Less common effects include prolonged redness, blistering, infection, or a change in skin pigment.

Medium and deeper skin tones, common across Malaysia, carry a higher chance of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation after energy-based treatment. This is why doctors here often choose gentler settings and longer intervals between sessions.
Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen is part of the plan for every treatment listed above, both before and after.

Ice-pick scarring rarely resolves fully with energy devices alone. Acne can recur after treatment, because treating marks or scars does not change the tendency to break out. Improvement builds gradually over months as collagen remodels.

risks.disclose: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, take or recently took oral acne medication, have a history of cold sores, keloid scarring or recent tanning, or have had any skin procedure in the past few weeks. Any of these may change what is appropriate or when.

costFactors.intro: Pricing is set after assessment. It depends on:
factors: What is being treated: marks generally need a different approach from structural scarring.
The area: full face, targeted zone, or back and chest.
The treatment and device: different platforms have different session structures.
How many sessions: set after assessment, and adjusted at review as your skin responds.
Whether treatments are combined: mixed scarring sometimes responds better to more than one modality.

faqs.a: Depressed scarring can often be improved, though rarely erased. How much improvement is realistic depends heavily on scar type: rolling and boxcar scars usually respond better than ice-pick scars, which are narrow and deep. See the acne scars page for each scar type.

Adult acne is usually multi-factorial. Hormonal fluctuation is a frequent contributor, particularly for women with breakouts around the jawline and chin that follow a cycle. It's also common for adult acne to look different from teenage acne: fewer spots, but deeper and slower to settle.

faqs.q: Will treatment make my acne worse first?
faqs.a: Some medical acne treatments involve an initial adjustment period where the skin appears worse before it improves. Energy-based treatments don't typically cause a flare, but they can leave redness or dryness for a few days.

faqs.q: Is laser treatment safe for darker or Asian skin tones?
faqs.a: Yes, when the device and settings are chosen appropriately by a doctor who is experienced with your skin type. The specific concern with medium and deeper skin tones is post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, the skin responding to treatment by producing extra pigment. It's a real consideration, not a reason to avoid treatment.

faqs.q: Can I wear makeup after treatment?
faqs.a: After minimal-downtime treatments, makeup can usually be applied the following day. After RF microneedling, most people wait until the redness settles, typically two to three days. After resurfacing laser, longer: the skin needs to re-epithelialise first.

faqs.q: Will my acne come back after treatment?
faqs.a: Possibly. Acne is a chronic condition for many people, with periods of flare and quiet. That's why the plan usually includes a maintenance element: appropriate daily skincare, sun protection, and ongoing medical management where indicated.

faqs.q: Do I need to stop my current skincare or acne medication?
faqs.a: Don't stop anything without telling your doctor first. Some products, retinoids and exfoliating acids in particular, are usually paused for a period before and after energy-based treatment.

Most people describe energy-based treatments as uncomfortable rather than painful. Topical numbing cream is applied beforehand where appropriate, and cooling is used during and after. RF microneedling is generally felt more than pico laser.
